slides.0.title: Gaillac and Fronton
slides.0.subtitle: Diversity on the Tarn and Négrette north of Toulouse
slides.1.title: Gaillac's history
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Ancient roots
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Viticulture dates to the 1st century AD, with Roman pottery found at Montans; the Abbey of Saint-Michel was founded in 972 (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The rooster mark
slides.1.highlights.1.content: In 1387 the Counts of Toulouse granted the right to mark barrels with a rooster emblem (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: AOC
slides.1.highlights.2.content: White gained AOC on 21 March 1938 and red on 23 October 1970; a quality renaissance began in the 1980s (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: Gaillac is one of the oldest wine districts in the South-West.
slides.2.title: Gaillac's varieties and rules
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Whites
slides.2.highlights.0.content: At least one of Len de l'El, Mauzac, Mauzac Rosé and Muscadelle, together at least 50%; Ondenc is also a key white variety (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Reds
slides.2.highlights.1.content: At least two of Duras, Braucol (Fer), Prunelart and Syrah, together at least 70% (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Four terroirs
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Left-bank boulbènes, right-bank Premières Côtes clay-limestone, the Cordes limestone plateau and Cunac acid schists (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: One AOC holds white, red, rosé, sparkling and sweet styles.
slides.3.title: Gaillac's styles
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Méthode Gaillacoise
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Made only from Mauzac, with a single fermentation completed in the bottle and no added sugar, also called Méthode Ancestrale (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Gaillac Doux
slides.3.highlights.1.content: At least 70 g/L residual sugar; made by late harvest, noble rot or passerillage; the old names Liquoreux and Moelleux are no longer authorised (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Primeur
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Red made solely from Gamay, released on the third Thursday of November; red output is about 110,000–150,000 hL a year (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.content: Gaillac's strength is that it can do almost everything.
slides.4.title: Fronton and Négrette
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Location
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Wikipedia: about 35 km north of Toulouse across Haute-Garonne and Tarn-et-Garonne; red is about 85% and rosé about 15%
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Négrette share differs
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Wikipedia says at least 50% Négrette; Wine With Seth's grape page says 50–70% in Fronton and a 40% minimum in any wine; the sources differ, so this is not tested
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Style
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Négrette is low in acidity and tannin but deeply coloured, with violet, raspberry and licorice; Wine Folly also notes an "animal" character
slides.4.content: Négrette makes Fronton distinct from other southern reds.
